answer: In a geology data market, a plume of readings from one karst cave earns one payout even if its seller creates many agent names. The market issues a one-use token for a randomly chosen site and requires a signed measurement and escrow bond; auditors compare a basalt reference sample and timestamp before payment. Ten fake identities need ten distinct sites, instruments and bonds, while copied readings forfeit escrow. A funded operator can buy real capacity and colluding auditors can mislabel samples, so assignments and appeals need independent review.
